deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck is building combinatorial 2-dimensional cell complexes ('surfaces représentatives' X_0, X_1, X_1') that model a space of configurations of pseudo-lines. On the previous page the vocabulary is: 'stable' cells (probably generic, simple configurations), 'sous-stable' cells (codimension-one degenerations, adjacent to a stable one), and 'supercritique' cells D_i (strong degenerations, probably many pseudo-lines through one point). Each D_i carries a combinatorial polygon with 2n_i edges ('arêtes superficiellement orientées'). One cuts X_0 near a supercritical vertex s. Counting the 'bouts libres' (free ends) depends on parity. For n odd one gets exactly 2(n-1) free ends, as needed. For n even one gets 6(n-1), which is redundant. The proposed fix is to blow up each supercritical vertex into a small supercritical disc F_s. The edges must then be reglued using arcs on D̃_i, the inverse image of D_i.

This page:
(1) There is a 'particularly pretty way' to reglue the 2(n-1) free ends inside F_i. The result is a new surface X_1'. Its vertices lying on the supercritical faces have order 3; all other vertices have order 4, so it is square-like away from the discs. The coloured sketch labelled 'X_1' pour n=5' shows this: a circle (the boundary of F_s) with alternating red and yellow-green rays outside (the adjacent sous-stable and stable cells) and a red trivalent tree-like pattern inside joining the ends.
(2) Programme: make the specialisation cases explicit (in generalisation over the D̃_i). This must cover not only the sous-stable cells next to D_i but now also the neighbouring stable cells. These are specialisations of combinatorial length 2, which amounts to passing to the doubly iterated barycentric subdivision of the cell decomposition of the D̃ and D̃_i.
(3) Diagnosis of a shared defect of X_0, X_1, X_1'. They are meant to carry the configurations and also the local systems, i.e. the parallel transport, of the combinatorial polygons Pol(D). That transport is defined only on the complement of the supercritical vertices or faces, which are places of effective ramification (non-trivial monodromy).
(4) A second, 'probably related' defect: there are no natural maps between these surfaces inside X, except perhaps for X_1' (to be checked in detail).
(5) This motivates further variants. The next page gives X_3: blow up the supercritical vertices, add 'transition arcs of weight 2', and use the barycentric subdivision with 2(n-1) new order-4 vertices in the stable case.

In modern terms, the goal is a cellular model of a configuration or moduli space of pseudo-line arrangements. On this model the tautological 'polygon' local system should extend without ramification, and the various models should be related by natural maps.
errors: Nothing checkably wrong on this page. The order-3 / order-4 claim for X_1' is plausible: blowing a vertex up into a disc glued by a trivalent pattern creates order-3 vertices on the disc boundary. However, the sketch for n=5 has many more rays than the 2(n-1)=8 free ends, so the correspondence between rays and free ends is not clear from the image.
The parity count on the previous page is internally inconsistent: it says 'n impair' twice in the disc discussion. That is probably a slip for 'pair' in one place. This is not an issue on this page.

ideas.what: Desingularising a 2-dimensional combinatorial model by replacing each supercritical vertex with a small disc and regluing the free ends trivalently. This yields a surface whose vertices are order 4 except for order 3 on the new discs.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial blow-up / truncation of a cell complex (a polyhedral analogue of real blow-up, as in Fulton–MacPherson or De Concini–Procesi compactifications, or truncating a vertex of a polytope)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard technique; De Concini–Procesi wonderful models (1995); Fulton–MacPherson (1994)

ideas.what: Combinatorial polygons Pol(D) attached to configurations, forming a local system (parallel transport) over the model surface, with ramification at supercritical cells.
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy of the tautological local system over a configuration/realisation space; related to zonotopal tilings, allowable sequences (Goodman–Pollack) and higher Bruhat orders B(n,2) (Manin–Schechtman 1989)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions related tame-topology and moduli themes; unsure about any explicit pseudo-line discussion

ideas.what: Using the doubly iterated barycentric subdivision to encode specialisations of combinatorial length 2.
ideas.modern_name: Barycentric subdivision / order complex of a face poset (nerve of a specialisation poset)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) and the Esquisse use barycentric subdivisions and nerves of posets as models

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an explicit design problem. He wants a 2-dimensional cellular model of the space of pseudo-line configurations on which the local system of combinatorial polygons Pol(D) extends with no ramification at supercritical points, and between whose variants (X_0, X_1, X_1', X_3) natural comparison maps exist. He diagnoses that the existing models fail on both counts and suspects the two failures are related.
missed.quote: Le défaut commun à ces trois surfaces représentatives ... n'est défini ici que dans le complémentaire de l'ens. des sommets ou faces supercritiques, qui sont des lieux de ramification effective. Un autre défaut, sans doute apparenté ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is close in spirit to later work on cellular models of pseudo-line arrangement spaces (higher Bruhat orders, Salvetti-type complexes, flip graphs and their 2-cells). It is also close to monodromy of tautological objects over oriented-matroid realisation spaces. The explicit link between removing ramification and the existence of comparison maps between models is not, as far as I know, stated in that literature. It is a modest but genuine unpursued thread.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working note: a desingularisation of a combinatorial surface, a programme of subdivisions, and a clear diagnosis of defects (ramified monodromy, no maps between models). It is interesting as documentation of Grothendieck's little-studied pseudo-line project, but it contains no finished result that is clearly absent from the literature.
